target_customer: Consumers and clinicians wanting quantitative whole-body MRI analysis (muscle and fat volumes in a 3D model)
problem: MRI scans were analyzed manually. Klarismo used machine learning to turn a full-body MRI into an annotated cloud 3D model with automatic volumetric tissue measurements.
product_category: MRI analysis software and consumer body imaging

founders.name: Marcus Foster
previous_startups: KAYMO (founder and CEO per YC bio)
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he led product teams at these companies, with no dates, so some may postdate Klarismo. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required machine learning segmentation of full-body MRI trained on proprietary labeled data, plus cloud processing at scale, hard for a small team in 2015.

defensibility.rationale: YC describes models trained on proprietary labeled MRI data, which could compound, but regulatory clearance and scan access were hard and unsourced here.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated source found on incumbents in 2015 and no sign of any acquisition.

market_need_then: No dated source found on demand for quantitative whole-body MRI in 2015; later companies such as Prenuvo and Ezra emerged years afterward.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Your body, reimagined' per a directory listing

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name is invented and unusual, which aids distinctiveness but no evidence shows it drove awareness.

outcome_analysis: Klarismo joined YC in Summer 2015 with about ten people and raised a seed round whose size sources dispute, then became inactive. A directory says it wound down by about February 2019 and a secondary profile blames high MRI costs and a niche market, but neither is a primary source, so the cause is not confirmed and no failure factors are asserted. The founder's YC bio now lists a later company, KAYMO, with no sourced link to Klarismo.
notes: No company website exists in the directory, so none was fetched. The healthcarediscovery.ai page and the Form D details were not opened because the fetch safety check was rate limited; its contents come from a search summary, and an EDGAR search found no Klarismo Form D. The $2.1M figure (Form D notices dated 2015-07-24 totaling about $2.1M from four investors) rests on that single directory. The $250K figure rests on StartupIntros alone, and CB Insights shows $2.22M over three rounds with a seed dated 2015-08-20 and no amount per round. The two recorded rounds may overlap or be the same financing; amounts conflict. Sources suggest a London base and a co-founder named Jack Kreindler but this was not confirmed from an opened source, so he is not recorded. Dated 2015 competitors were not found, so the list is empty.
